h: Getting the Best From an Xscape Day
p: The trick with Xscape is not trying to do everything at once. With so much under one roof, it's easy to get carried away and end up with tired kids and a lighter wallet. Pick one or two main activities, book those ahead where you can, and then let the rest of the day fill itself in around them.

Getting there is fairly simple. Xscape sits at the eastern end of central Milton Keynes, and while it's a fair walk from Milton Keynes Central station along the boulevards, buses and taxis make it a short hop. If you're driving, the town centre's grid layout makes it easier to find than you'd think, though parking can fill up on busy weekends.

Right next door is the Theatre District, home to Milton Keynes Theatre and MK Gallery, which puts on changing exhibitions in its bold modern building. It's a good calm option for grown-ups while the teenagers stay in Xscape. Beyond that, Campbell Park rolls down towards the Grand Union Canal, with sculptures, wide lawns and big views across the city from the top.

For families, a nice routine is to do the active bit in the morning, grab lunch inside the building, then head out to Campbell Park in the afternoon for some fresh air before home time. Teenagers and groups of mates can happily spend the whole day hopping between venues inside.
Whatever you plan, check opening details for each individual venue before you go. They're run separately, and the line-up does change.
